cases.note: The loop iterates thresholds in the same PB→KB order and picks the first matching unit, defaulting to 'B', exactly matching the original if/else chain. No observable behaviour change.

The diff changes the core schema's explicit integer pattern from [-+]?0b[0-1]+ to [^-+]?0b[0-1]+, so explicitly tagged negative/positive binary integers like '-0b101' are now rejected by the core schema, which previously resolved them via parseYamlInteger$2.

cases.note: Equivalent refactor: hoisting digits.slice(2) into `rest` yields the same arguments to parseInt in every branch; the decimal path still uses the sign-stripped `digits`. No observable behaviour change.

The diff replaces the `type === 'string'` check with `true`, so any non-string value with a truthy `length` (arrays, objects with length) is passed to parse instead of throwing, and strings are no longer type-verified.
